q: Which command shows the folder you are in?
explain: pwd = print working directory.

q: How do you go back to your home folder?
explain: cd with no argument goes home (same as cd ~).

q: Which command lists hidden files too?
explain: -a shows every file, including names starting with a dot.

q: What does `mkdir -p a/b/c` do?
choices: Creates a, b and c as needed
explain: -p creates the missing parents and doesn't complain if they exist.

q: Which symbol sends a command's output to a file, replacing it?
explain: > overwrites the file; >> appends to it.

q: What does `|` do between two commands?
choices: Sends the output of the first into the second
Runs them at the same time, unrelated
Runs the second only if the first fails
Writes the output to a file
explain: A pipe connects stdout of the left command to stdin of the right one.

q: Which key completes a command or file name?
explain: Tab completes; press it twice to see all the choices.

q: How do you see the manual of a command?
explain: man opens the manual page; q quits it.

q: What does `$?` hold right after a command?
explain: 0 means success, anything else is an error.

q: Which command prints a text?
explain: echo prints its arguments; cat prints files.

q: What does `rm -r folder` do?
choices: Deletes the folder and everything in it
explain: rm has no trash: -r deletes recursively, for good.

q: How do you run the previous command again?
explain: !! expands to the last command (sudo !! reruns it with sudo).

q: What does `cmd 2>&1` do?
choices: Sends errors where the normal output goes
explain: 2 is stderr, 1 is stdout: 2>&1 merges them.

q: What is `$(date)` inside a command?
choices: The output of date, inserted there
explain: $( ) is command substitution.

q: Which loop runs for each .log file?
explain: The glob *.log expands to the matching file names.

q: What does `set -e` do in a script?
choices: Stops the script at the first failing command
explain: set -e exits on error; set -x prints each command.

q: How do you read a file line by line safely?
choices: while IFS= read -r line; do …; done < file
explain: for over $(cat) splits on spaces, not lines.

q: What does `&&` do in `make && ./app`?
choices: Runs both at the same time
explain: && continues on success, || on failure.

q: Why quote "$var"?
choices: So spaces in it don't split it into several words
explain: Unquoted variables are split on spaces and expanded as globs.

q: Which command makes a script runnable?
explain: The x permission lets you run it with ./script.sh.

q: What does `<<EOF` start?
choices: A heredoc: lines until EOF are the input
explain: Handy to feed several lines to a command.

q: What does `jobs` show?
choices: Commands running in the background of this shell
explain: fg brings one back, bg resumes it in the background.
